candidates.tagline: Universal spent $550M on a kids' theme park that guests say looks like a maximum-security prison
candidates.story: Universal Kids Resort, a $550M children's theme park in Frisco, Texas built for ages 3–8, opened for previews in June 2026 to find that vast stretches of bare concrete, minimal shade, and almost no theming left guests comparing it to 'a maximum-security prison in Texas' — with the official July 1 opening still days away.
candidates.why_funny: Designers promised lush storybook lands full of Shrek and SpongeBob magic, delivered what guests called 'McDonald's landscaping: the ride,' and chose to build it in one of the hottest cities in America with virtually no shade.
candidates.alt: Wide exterior view of Universal Kids Resort in Frisco, Texas showing broad concrete plazas with sparse theming and limited landscaping under bright Texas sun

candidates.tagline: Man builds 23-foot driveable banana car; has been pulled over hundreds of times because the banana blocks his plate
candidates.story: Steve Braithwaite's Big Banana Car — a 23-foot fiberglass banana mounted on a 1993 Ford F-150 — was pulled over again on I-90 near Billings, Montana on June 24, 2026 because cargo boxes partially blocked his 'SPLIT' license plate, continuing a 15-year tradition: he says he was 'the most pulled-over man in America' for the first eight years of driving it.
candidates.why_funny: He built a vehicle specifically designed to look like a giant banana, expected to drive it legally across America, and is still surprised it keeps attracting police attention — the banana shape physically prevents proper license plate display.
candidates.alt: Montana Highway Patrol trooper standing beside a 23-foot bright yellow fiberglass banana-shaped car pulled over on the shoulder of Interstate 90 near Billings
